column3: “The days of David drew near” is rendered “David’s time … drew near.”
“Become a man” is rendered “show yourself a man,” and NASB adds “therefore.”
“Cause to prosper” is rendered “succeed.”
“His word” is rendered “His promise,” “descendants” as “sons,” and “faithfulness” as “truth”; “will not be cut off to you” becomes “you shall not lack.”
“Put bloods of war in peace” is rendered “shed the blood of war in peace.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Loyalty” is rendered “kindness,” and “drew near to me” as “assisted me.”
The oath form “if I will put you to death” is rendered “I will not put you to death.”
“Leave unpunished” is rendered “let him go unpunished.”
“Lay down” is rendered “slept.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“A word is mine to you” is rendered “I have something to say to you.”
“Set their faces to me” is rendered “expected me.”
“Do not turn away my face” is rendered “do not refuse me.”
Close to the Hebrew; “turn away your face” is rendered “refuse you.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Placed a throne” is rendered “had a throne set.”
“Turn away my face” is rendered “refuse me.”
Close to the Hebrew.
NASB adds “also” and “even.”
NASB supplies “not” and “against” in the oath (“if Adonijah has not spoken … against his own life”).
“Appointed me” is rendered “established me,” and “spoke” as “promised.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“A man of death” is rendered “you deserve to die,” and “this day” as “at this time.”
“Drove out” is rendered “dismissed.”
“Turned aside after” is rendered “followed.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Indeed” is rendered “No, for.”
